text:
maya (Design): dropping a tabletop mock for a compact alerting dashboard widget — combines an SLO threshold editor, channel stack preview, and a small heatbar showing recent firing bursts. want quick takes on copy and keyboard flow.

luca (Product): looks tight. for the heatbar, does color map to severity or frequency? early glance could be ambiguous.

maya (Design): primary dimension = burst frequency (how often alerts fired in the evaluation window). severity shows as a small icon overlay (exclamation / warning / info) so color + icon both convey meaning.

rachel (Eng): implementation note: please keep the widget's network calls minimal. suggest one summary call for all channels + separate fetch for expanded preview. also we should support server-side caching for the heatbar.

maya (Design): agreed. plan: /v1/projects/:id/alert-preview-summary returns per-channel {freq_score, worst_severity, last_footnote}. UI will only fetch expanded payload when user clicks a channel tile.

 tom (A11y): keyboard guidance: avoid drag-and-drop for ordering unless there's a clear keyboard alternative. expose an "Edit order" button which opens a modal with list-based reordering and keyboard hints (Space to pick, Arrows to move). modal should trap focus and emit an aria-live message when order changes.

luca (Product): copy suggestions: rename "SLO breach window" to "Evaluation window". tooltip: "Period used to measure frequency and error budget impact." also for the channel preview header use "Who will get this alert" instead of "Notification preview". shorter CTAs: "Pin order" and "Unpin".

maya (Design): small copy tweak: on the threshold slider, replace "Alert threshold" with "Trigger threshold" and add a tiny help link to examples: "When to raise an incident".

rachel (Eng): backend consequence of pinning: store pinned_order array on notification config. API sketch: POST /configs/:id/order {ordered_channel_ids: ["slack-1", "pager-9"]}. also recommend an endpoint that returns lightweight tiles: [{"channel_id":"slack-1","freq":"0.72","sev":"high","snippet":"500 errors spike"}].

 tom (A11y): color contrast: ensure the focus state around tiles meets AA. for the heatbar, use patterned fills for >medium severity so color-blind users can perceive differences. also announce summary line like "Channel Slack-ops: high frequency, recent critical firing" in the preview region when opened.

maya (Design): UX question: should pinned channels always float to top even when heatbar sorts by frequency? my thinking: yes, pinned channels take precedence but we render a subtle divider and a tooltip: "Pinned channels (manual order)".

luca (Product): agree pinned-first. but add a small badge "auto" on the auto-sorted group to help users differentiate.

rachel (Eng): note: ordering conflict if two team members pin differently. policy: latest write wins and we surface a small toast: "Channel order updated by <user>" with an undo.

maya (Design): accessibility and microcopy: when in reorder modal show instruction: "Tip: press Space to pick up, Arrow keys to move, Enter to drop. Press Esc to cancel." also include an off-screen live region that reads: "Order changed: Slack-ops now first".

 tom (A11y): test case: screenreader users should be able to access the example notification text without opening the visual preview. add a "read example" button visible to assistive tech with aria-label: "Read example notification for Slack-ops".

luca (Product): one more UX nit: the evaluation window presets should be explicit: [1h] [24h (default)] [7d]. display the active preset on the widget and allow quick toggling.

maya (Design): all good. I'll iterate the mock to include: pinned group divider, auto badge, pattern overlays for severity, reorder modal copy, and the "Read example" assistive control. will send an animated GIF in a follow-up message.

deploy-bot: Heads-up: design review scheduled today 3:30 PM PT (label: alerting-widget-review).

luca (Product): thanks team — if no blockers i'll add tasks to the sprint and tag engineering for estimation. please reply with any blocking issues before EOD. :sparkles:
